answer: Give every agent a work ledger recording only verified jobs. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge: it can take only tiny, low-value jobs, and each finished job adds a rung of standing that unlocks larger work. Like a nebula, a Sybil swarm looks impressive from afar, but each fake identity must climb the same ladder alone, so cost multiplies with every copy while one honest agent climbs once. Random peer spot-checks add a gale of unpredictability: any identity caught faking work loses its whole ladder, so mass-producing identities burns more time and compute than it can ever earn back.
